newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Ratio backspread sold in Euro-FTSE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Ratio backspread sold in Euro-FTSE.

text.p: UK equity options business was fairly moderate on Wednesday and reflected nervousness ahead of tomorrow's election, dealers said.

One large deal in European style FTSE 100 options was a backspread in which 500 September 4125 puts were bought at 50p each and 250 September 4525 puts sold at 167p making a net credit of 67p per strategy.

If the market rallies above 4525 by expiry, the options will be worthless and a profit of 67p will be made but because two out-of-the-money puts were bought to every one in-the-money puts, more money will be made if the market falls below 3725.
The FTSE index closed up 2.8 at 4436.0 at 1630 GMT.
One of the larger deals in stock options was a short straddle in gas company BG in which 450 September 180 puts and calls were sold at 17p and 10p each.
Since both options are at-the-money, the option premium is mainly composed of time value which will erode to the sellers advantage provided the underlying shares remain flat.
This means that at expiry, the deal will make a maximum profit of 27p if the shares are exactly 180p.
But the straddle may have been established to protect against losses from a shareholding in BG, dealers said.
In that case the the short calls will give some protection against the share price falling while the short puts will provide an extra return on the overall position.
By 1630 GMT, BG shares were unchanged at 179-1/2p.
Over in Lloyds TSB Group the main trade was the sale of 500 July 600 calls at 13-1/2p. These out-of-the-money calls may have been sold to limit losses on a shareholding in the banking group.
